sup:70110.body:
Guten Tag,

Thank you for your enquiry. Please find our Angebot below. For many years, our family foundry has taken great pride in supplying your respected company with high-quality castings from our region, and we value our long standing relationship very much.

Our team has prepared our offer carefully. We can offer you a price of €138.55 per unit, valid from 1 November 2026. This Angebot remains valid for 30 days.

To remain transparent about our situation, LCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 30 % of our cost. Furthermore, PPI-C241 rose 6.5 % in twelve months and is 24 % of our cost. We trust that you understand the necessity of these figures for our ongoing operation and quality standards.

Viele Grüße aus der Gießerei
Thomas Brandlhuber
Owner, Gießerei Brandlhuber GmbH & Co. KG

sup:70110.body:
Simulated supplier. Dear Purchasing Team,

Thank you for your thoughtful reply. We take your comments on delivery performance and quality seriously and are working on both.

On costs: our casting input costs are driven largely by materials and energy, not only the indices you cite, so we cannot go all the way to the level your weighted view suggests. We are willing to move, though, as a sign of our long relationship. We will not give you a ranked list of fallback offers, but here are two options, both effective 1 November 2026 with a 12-month term, 42 days lead time and FCA:

* Option A: EUR 138.55 per unit with payment in 30 days.
* Option B: EUR 135.78 per unit with payment in 30 days, which is a real concession on our side.

If timing of the increase matters to you, we are happy to discuss it further, but a later effective date would come at a higher price. Please tell us which option works for you.

Best regards,
Thomas Brandlhuber
Owner, Gießerei Brandlhuber GmbH & Co. KG

sup:70110.subject: Re: Price adjustment HN 50-200 - proposal for a balanced package
sup:70110.body:
Dear Mr. Brandlhuber,

Thank you for moving on price. We want a healthy, stable supply, and we know quicker payment matters to you, so we would like to meet you on that.

On the numbers, the weighted view of your cost drivers (LCI-C +2.7%, PPI-C241 +6.5%, PPI-D351 -3.7%, at the weights you cited and our own) gives a cost increase of about 2.3%, well below 9.5%. Delivery (OTD about 85%) and quality (712 ppm) are also below expectations, and the scorecard is now amber.

To reach a balanced agreement we propose the following package, which includes the faster payment you asked for:
* Unit price: EUR 131.00
* Effective date: 2027-01-01
* Payment days: 14

Other terms stay as in your offer: 12 months, 42 days lead time, FCA, and quantity of 8150 pcs per year.

Could you tell us your best position on this package, or on any combination of unit price, effective date and payment days that you prefer? We are keen to find a solution that works for both sides.

Best regards,
Purchasing, Hollerau Pumpenwerke

sup:70110.subject: Re: Brandlhuber announces +9.5 % on HN volute casings
sup:70110.body:
Simulated supplier. Dear Purchasing Team,

Thank you for your proposal and for the offer of faster payment, which we do value. Your weighted calculation understates our position, however. Castings are driven by metal, energy and labour, and our costs have not fallen the way one index suggests. We cannot reach EUR 131.00, even with 14-day payment and a January start.

We can offer two alternatives, both for 12 months, 42 days lead time, FCA and 8,150 pcs per year:

* Option 1: EUR 135.78 per unit, effective 1 November 2026, payment in 30 days.
* Option 2: EUR 135.78 per unit, effective 1 January 2027, payment in 14 days. This gives you the later start you were looking for and gives us the faster payment.

This is a genuine move from our opening quote of EUR 138.55. We have taken your comments on delivery and quality seriously and are working on both. Please tell us which option suits you.

Best regards,
Thomas Brandlhuber
Owner, Gießerei Brandlhuber GmbH & Co. KG

sup:70110.subject: Re: Price adjustment HN 50-200 - our proposal
sup:70110.body:
Dear Mr. Brandlhuber,

Thank you for the further move to EUR 135.78 and for your flexibility on timing. We want a healthy, stable supply and are ready to give you the faster payment you asked for.

Your Option 2 (EUR 135.78, 1 January 2027, 14 days) is still well above what the cost evidence supports. The weighted view of your cost drivers is about +2.3%, which points to roughly EUR 129 to 132. Delivery (OTD about 85%) and quality (712 ppm) also remain below expectations.

To close the gap we propose the following package, which gives you 14-day payment and a clean January start:
* Unit price: EUR 132.27
* Effective date: 2027-01-01
* Payment days: 14

Other terms stay as in your offer: 12 months, 42 days lead time, FCA, 8,150 pcs per year.

Could you tell us your best position on this package? If EUR 132.27 is not possible, please state your best price for 1 January 2027 with 14-day payment, so we can find common ground.

Best regards,
Purchasing, Hollerau Pumpenwerke

sup:70510.subject: Re: Nordmark passes on copper for the 7.5 kW motor
sup:70510.body:
Simulated supplier. Dear Hollerau Purchasing team,

Thank you for your reply. We will not disclose a sequence of fallback or final offers. Instead, here are three binding alternatives, each with a different trade-off between price, payment terms and copper-risk sharing. All are DAP, 35 days lead time, 12 months from 1 January 2027, 6,110 units per year:

1) Fixed price: €370.96 per unit, 30 days net, no index clause. This gives you full price certainty, and we carry the copper risk.

2) Index-linked: €370.96 per unit, 30 days net, CU-NOTATION clause (20% material share, base month August 2026) with a 3% deadband.

3) Index-linked: €370.96 per unit, 14 days net, CU-NOTATION clause (20% material share, base month August 2026) with a 5% deadband.

CU-NOTATION is up 47.7% over twelve months and makes up 20% of our cost, so we have little room on price. If you want to discuss a different payment term or clause, tell us what matters most to you and we will review what we can do within the group's commercial guidelines.

Best regards,
Petra Lechner
Key Account Manager, Antriebstechnik Nordmark AG

sup:70510.subject: Re: Binding alternatives - our position and counter-proposal
sup:70510.body:
Dear Ms Lechner,

Thank you for the three binding alternatives and the cost background. We value the long relationship and want a stable supply for 2027.

We see the 6.5% increase as well above what the facts support. Our settlements with you in recent years were 1.2-1.4%. Copper is a real factor, but at about 20% of cost it explains only part of the increase. Your own letter tells us price changes up to 2% need no pricing committee approval, which would make a quick agreement easy.

We would like to propose a package that gives you volume certainty (6,110 pcs, 12 months from 1 January 2027, DAP) in return for a more moderate price. We would like to hear your best position on each term:

- Unit price: our proposal is EUR 362.44 per piece, about 2.3% above today's price.
- Payment days: we can discuss 14 days if the price works; otherwise 60 days.
- Index clause: we prefer none. If you require one, it would need a 5% deadband and a lower base price.

Proposed package: EUR 362.44, 60 days net, no index clause.

Please tell us what you can do on price, payment days and index clause, so that we can reach an agreement soon.

Best regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing

sup:70510.subject: Re: Nordmark passes on copper for the 7.5 kW motor
sup:70510.body:

Thank you for your proposal and for the commitment to 6,110 units over 12 months. We value the relationship and want to find a solution, but at EUR 362.44 with 60 days net and no index clause we cannot go along. Copper is up 47.7% over twelve months, and without an index clause we carry that risk for the full year. We also need to stay within the group's commercial guidelines, and I cannot claim any approval beyond what I can offer here.

Here are three binding alternatives (all DAP, 35 days lead time, 12 months from 1 January 2027, 6,110 units per year):

1) EUR 370.96 per unit, 30 days net, no index clause (full price certainty for you).

2) EUR 370.96 per unit, 45 days net, no index clause (an extended payment term in exchange for the fixed price).

3) EUR 363.54 per unit, 30 days net, no index clause. This is a movement of about 2% on price. It is our best price for 30 days net without an index clause.

If payment term matters more to you than price, option 2 gives you 15 extra days. If you can move to a price in this range, we can close quickly.

Best regards,
Petra Lechner
Key Account Manager, Antriebstechnik Nordmark AG

Thank you for your reply and your interest in a long-term renewal. I will not rank offers as "best and final" at this stage, but I can show how the terms trade against each other. All offers are DAP, with a 49-day lead time and an effective date of 1 January 2027.

1) Our current quote, which matches your stated need: 4580 pcs per year, 12 months, 30 days net, at €438.21 per unit.

Your 36-month option at 4580 pcs and 30 days net (EUR 429.45) is the closest to our needs. It is still well above our current price of EUR 412.74, and your own sales director signalled openness on payment terms. We therefore propose the following package:

* Unit price: EUR 419.61
* Payment: 60 days net
* Contract term: 24 months
* Volume: 4580 pcs per year
* DAP, 49-day lead time, effective 1 January 2027

This is a firm volume commitment with a longer term, which gives you planning security for capacity and material purchasing. The price is about 2% below your 36-month quote, which stays within what we understand your pricing committee can handle.

1) 4580 pcs per year, 36 months, 30 days net, €429.45 per unit. This is the 36-month option from my last email, unchanged.

2) 4580 pcs per year, 24 months, 30 days net, €416.30 per unit. I can only do this if the price is paired with a firm commitment to the full volume. It is a closer match to your preferred term, but a lower price on a shorter commitment than option 1 is a real concession on our side, and it is subject to our formal confirmation.

3) 5496 pcs per year, 36 months, 45 days net, €409.67 per unit. This is the lowest price we can support, and it needs both the higher volume and the three-year term.

Thank you for your message. I will not rank offers as "first" or "final", but I am happy to show where we have flexibility. Our price depends mainly on contract term and payment terms, and a longer commitment gives us planning security on 20,000 pcs per year.

Option A: EUR 4.96 per unit, 30 days net, 12 months.
Option B: EUR 4.96 per unit, 30 days net, 24 months. This secures the price for a longer period, with no index adjustment during the term.
Option C: EUR 4.86 per unit, 30 days net, 36 months. This is our strongest price for a three-year commitment with standard payment terms.

Regarding the indices: the 65% PPI weighting rose only 0.8%, but labour, logistics, and DAP delivery with a 7-day lead time are also part of our cost base, so we can not move far below the current level. Longer payment terms would need to be reflected in price, as they cost us financing.

If one of these suits you, please tell me which and we will finalise the renewal for 1 January 2027.

Best regards,
Florian Gruber
Inside Sales, Wälzlager-Zentrum Süd GmbH

sup:70620.subject: Renewal 6306-2Z C3 - our position on price and term
sup:70620.body:
Dear Mr Gruber,

Thank you for the three options. None of them yet reflects the cost picture you describe. By your own weighting, PPI-C2815 (65%, +0.8%) and LCI-C (10%, +2.7%) imply a cost increase of well under 1% on the current 4.39. Your own quote 7200019 of 20 September was 4.63. An increase to 4.96 is therefore hard for us to justify.

We do want to consolidate and are prepared to commit 20,000 pcs per year for a multi-year term, and we would also consider 36 months. In return we need a price that tracks your actual cost development. Quality has also slipped in recent quarters (ppm around 300, OTD around 85%), which weighs on our total cost.

Could you tell me the best unit price you can offer for 24 months and for 36 months at each of the payment terms 30, 45, 60 and 90 days? The owner kindly offered to walk us through your calculation (hourly rates and material). I would welcome that if it helps close the gap. If you cannot give a range, please send the best complete offer you can make across all three terms.

Best regards,
Purchasing, Hollerau Pumpenwerke

sup:70620.body:

Regarding the quality figures you mention, we take them seriously and would be glad to review them with you, as reliable delivery is part of what we want to offer in a long-term relationship.

Here is where we can go, as a commitment on 20,000 pcs per year from 1 January 2027:

- EUR 4.96 per unit, 30 days net, 24 months, with no index adjustment during the term.
- EUR 4.86 per unit, 30 days net, 36 months. This is our strongest price at standard payment terms.
- EUR 4.86 per unit, 45 days net, 12 months, as an alternative if you prefer a shorter term.

Prices for longer payment terms do not come out lower; extended terms cost us financing, so we would not reduce price while extending them. If you would like to go through the calculation in person, we are happy to arrange a call with the owner. Please tell me which option suits you.

Best regards,

sup:70410.body:

The EUR 32.20 per unit is not workable for us. It is well above our current price, and the cost basis for this seal does not support such an increase. Your own history shows renewal requests of about 2% or less, and price changes above 2% need your pricing committee.

In return for a firm 24-month commitment on the full 23,400 pcs per year, with a 35-day lead time, we propose EUR 27.50 per unit. Payment is 30 days net, DAP, effective 2027-01-01, as before. This gives you planning certainty on a capacity-constrained allocation.

This is a binding proposal. Could you confirm it, or tell us which term prevents you from doing so, and give us your best price on each of the 24- and 36-month terms?

Best regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing

sup:70410.subject: Re: Ravensteiner cuts the seal allocation
sup:70410.body:

We have moved from our earlier EUR 32.20. Here are our best prices for the full 23,400 pcs per year. All options are DAP, 30 days net, effective 2027-01-01:

* Option B: 36 months, 35-day lead time, EUR 29.91 per unit. The longer commitment secures your allocation for three years.

We can offer the longer commitment you prefer. Our proposal is a firm 36-month commitment on the full 23,400 pcs per year, a 35-day lead time, EUR 28.40 per unit, 30 days net, DAP, effective 2027-01-01. This gives you three years of planning certainty on a capacity-constrained allocation.

You asked about faster payment. We can pay in 14 days, which is a real cash-flow gain for you. In exchange, we ask for a later effective date, so that our planning and our own customer pricing can adjust.

Our proposal: EUR 130.50 per unit, effective 1 January 2027, payment in 14 days, with the 12-month term, 8,150 pieces per year, 42-day lead time and FCA unchanged. This also gives you a firm commitment to the full annual volume.

Could you please confirm whether you can meet this, or tell us your best offer on each of the three terms (unit price, effective date, payment days)? Please also repeat any binding options you are prepared to keep, so we can compare them like for like.

Thank you for your reply. We will not label offers as first, second or final, but here are two concrete alternatives for your volume of 23,700 per year, DAP, 14 days lead time, from 1 January 2027, no tooling:

* Option A: EUR 6.10 per unit, 30 days net, 12 months, no index clause. This is our quote as sent and it stays available.
* Option B: EUR 5.98 per unit, 30 days net, 12 months, no index clause. This is a price reduction in exchange for a fixed price and no escalation clause.
* Option C: EUR 5.98 per unit, 14 days net, 24 months, no index clause. Here the longer commitment and faster payment support the lower price.

On the trade-offs: price is what we move on when you give us a longer term, faster payment, or a fixed price without an index clause. Longer payment terms and an index clause with a deadband work against a lower price, because we carry the cost and the raw material risk.

On the basis of the increase: alloy (AS-14404) is 45 % of our cost and rose 5.9 % over twelve months. PPI-C2431 is 38 % of our cost and rose 12.3 %, and LCI-C is 5 % and rose 2.7 %. Taken together, this drives our cost up by more than the alloy figure alone suggests. We are happy to go through this in detail by phone. We can only speak to the 6.06 quote you mention if you send us the reference, as it predates the current cost basis.

Please tell us which option, or which combination of terms, is closest to what you need.

Best regards,
Franz Seidl
Inside Sales, Blankstahl Werdenfels GmbH

A cost-based view: alloy AS-14404 rose 5.9 % and is about 45 % of your cost, which is roughly 2.7 % on total cost. Even if PPI and labour are added, the justified increase is far below the 4.5 % you are asking over our current 5.84 EUR. Over the last three years our renewals settled 4 to 6 % below the opening asks.

We can offer a longer commitment (24 or 36 months) and a fixed price without an index clause, but only against a clearly lower unit price and payment terms of 45 to 60 days. Please send us your best offer for each of these combinations, with every term stated:

We looked at the cost drivers you named. Over twelve months, LCI-C rose 2.7% and PPI-C241 rose 6.5%. Weighted by your own cost shares, and including the other input series, this supports an increase of roughly 2-3%, not 9.5%. To meet you halfway, we can offer what you asked for: fast payment (14 days, instead of our usual 60) and a firm commitment to the full 12-month volume of 8,150 pieces. In exchange we propose:

- Effective date: 2027-01-01

We will not rank our offers as a sequence of fallbacks. Here are two concrete options, both DAP, 5-day lead time, effective 1 January 2027:

Option A: 24-month contract, 30 days net, €5.74 per kit. This keeps our opening price but gives you two years of price stability and secured supply for the volume.

Option B: 12-month contract, 30 days net, €5.63 per kit. This is a reduction from our opening quote, with the shorter commitment you may prefer.

The price improvement reflects the bundled volume. Longer payment terms or further reductions would need a correspondingly longer commitment. Please tell us which option suits you, or which term matters most to you, and we will review it.

Best regards,

Inside Sales, Schraubenhandel Leitner & Sohn GmbH

Best regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing

sup:70610.subject: Re: Bundle the fastener kit with one distributor

sup:70710.body:
Simulated supplier. Dear Hollerau Pumpenwerke Purchasing team,

Thank you for your reply. We appreciate that your nickel and alloy needs are covered at fixed prices until March 2027. Our volume starts on 1 January 2027, so the fixed cover only partly overlaps with our own raw material exposure. For that reason I will not offer a surcharge, and I will keep this to simple fixed-price structures without an index clause.

I am not going to share a ranked sequence of offers, but here are three options. Each is a fixed price, with no index clause and no surcharge:

* Option A: EUR 6.05 per unit, 30 days net, 12 months, no index clause.
* Option B: EUR 5.75 per unit, 30 days net, 24 months, no index clause.
* Option C: EUR 5.75 per unit, 30 days net, 36 months, no index clause.

The longer terms allow us to plan material purchasing and capacity for your 94,800 units per year, which is why we can move on price in exchange for term. Delivery is DAP in 10 days, and there are no tooling costs.

sup:70710.body:
Dear Mr. Aigner,

Thank you for the three options. A 24-month term suits us, but the price does not yet reflect the facts:

* Your own quotation of 10 September 2026 (quote 7300008) was EUR 5.45 per unit, 10 days lead time, valid 90 days, with material covered until March 2027.
* Your nickel and alloy cover is fixed until March 2027, so there is no cost increase in the first quarter of the contract.
* We have a competing quote and a 24-month volume of 94,800 units per year to award.
